title: Make the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Act of 2025
official_title: To establish a program to Beautify the District of Columbia and establish the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Commission.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. McGuire (R-VA) with 4 cosponsors. A federal program directing immigration enforcement and law-enforcement coordination in the District would need 60 votes in the Senate and is likely to draw strong Democratic opposition over federal control of D.C., making passage unlikely.
summary: Creates a federal program to clean up the District of Columbia and a commission to coordinate federal law enforcement there, including immigration enforcement and support for the D.C. police.
brief: Establishes a federal D.C. beautification program and a commission to coordinate federal law enforcement and immigration enforcement in the District.

top_lines.headline: D.C. Beautification Program
subs: Interior Department program to clean up D.C. public spaces
Includes graffiti removal and monument restoration

top_lines.headline: Safe and Beautiful Commission
subs: Federal commission chaired by a White House official
Coordinates federal law enforcement and immigration enforcement in D.C.
Reviews D.C. sanctuary-city status and supports the D.C. police

items.main: Names the Act the “Make the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Act of 2025”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Program To Beautify District of Columbia

items.main: Directs the Interior Department to create a program to clean up and restore D.C. public spaces.
items.detail: Within 30 days, the Secretary of the Interior must develop a program — in consultation with the Attorney General, Transportation, the D.C. Mayor, the U.S. Attorney for D.C., and others — to coordinate cleanliness of federal and D.C. facilities, monuments, public spaces, and transit (including graffiti removal), restore, to the extent practicable, damaged or defaced District of Columbia and Federal monuments, and encourage private-sector participation. An annual report is required, and the program sunsets January 2, 2029.

sections.label: Section 3 — District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Commission

items.main: Establishes a federal commission to coordinate law enforcement in the District.
items.detail: Creates a Commission with members from Interior, Transportation, Homeland Security, the FBI, U.S. Marshals, ATF, U.S. Attorneys, and the Executive Office of the Mayor of D.C., chaired by a senior White House official. Its functions are to recommend and review actions on maximum enforcement of federal immigration law in D.C., monitor the District's sanctuary-city status, accredit the D.C. forensic crime lab, support recruitment and capabilities of the D.C. police, speed concealed-carry license processing, review pretrial-detention policies, address transit fare evasion, and expand federal and local law-enforcement presence in D.C., among other areas. The Commission reports to Congress and sunsets January 2, 2029.

criticisms.why: I strongly oppose this bill. I include in the Record letters opposing this bill from the District of Columbia Mayor and every member of the D.C. Council. September 10, 2025.

gaps: The bill directs maximum federal immigration enforcement in D.C. but does not provide funding for the additional law-enforcement activity.
It establishes a commission to recommend actions but the commission's recommendations are not binding on the District or federal agencies.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Norton
featured_quotes.text: I strongly oppose this bill. I include in the Record letters opposing this bill from the District of Columbia Mayor and every member of the D.C. Council. September 10, 2025.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Higgins
featured_quotes.text: I rise to support H.R. 5103. As a proud cosponsor of H.R. 5103, I stand with Representative McGuire and my Republican colleagues to deliver on President Trump's vision for our Nation's capital. This bill codifies Executive Order 14252 and turns words into law to make Washington, D.C., safe, clean, and beautiful once again.

added: Interior Department program to beautify D.C. (sunsets January 2, 2029)
District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Commission to coordinate federal law enforcement and immigration enforcement in D.C. (sunsets January 2, 2029)
Adds the Executive Office of the Mayor of the District of Columbia as a Commission member entity
Commission functions list reworded to be open-ended — "with respect to, but not limited to" the listed items
modified: Program purpose changed from establishing a plan to "establish and implement" a plan; monument restoration now covers "District of Columbia and Federal" monuments and is qualified "to the extent practicable"
Short title becomes "Make the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Act of 2025"
removed: Drops the United States Park Police from the list of authorities the Commission may request operational assistance from
